parts.text: Describe the features of the self-report method.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Design an alternative investigation into cognitive style and entry into physical sciences and
humanities courses as a longitudinal study, and describe how it could be conducted.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Evaluate this alternative way of studying cognitive style and entry into physical sciences and
humanities courses in methodological and ethical terms.

text: Billington et al. (empathising and systemising) conducted a snapshot self-report study to
investigate cognitive style and entry into physical sciences and humanities courses. An alternative
way to investigate this would be to conduct a longitudinal study.

parts.text: What is meant by the psychodynamic perspective?

parts.text:
Discuss the strengths and weaknesses of investigating the Oedipus complex using qualitative
data, using examples from the Freud study.

Section B (20 marks)
Answer one question in this section.

text: Freud conducted a case study to investigate the Oedipus complex in little Hans.

parts.text:
Outline what is meant by the term ‘ethical guideline’. 
Using the studies from the list below, answer the questions which follow:
Held and Hein (kitten carousel)
Rosenhan (sane in insane places)
Schachter and Singer (emotion)

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe how one ethical guideline was broken in each of these studies.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: What are the advantages when psychologists follow ethical guidelines in their studies?

Milgram (obedience)
Loftus and Pickrell (false memories)
Piliavin et al. (subway Samaritans)

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe how the data were collected in each of these studies.

What are the problems for psychologists in trying to conduct studies with ecological validity?
